answers:
IBM Cloudant legacy is a unique access control system for IBM Cloudant that requires individual sets of credentials for each service instance. It uses HTTP basic authentication with credentials that aren't bound to an individual user or service. Each user or service must have its own set of credentials to access a specific service instance.
Using IAM for IBM Cloudant provides several advantages, including managing access to IBM Cloudant with the standard tooling of IBM Cloud and using credentials that you can easily revoke and rotate when you use IBM Cloud IAM.

history.content: What is the subject of an access policy?
The subject of an access policy is the user, service ID, or access group that you are providing access.

An IAM access policy is a way to give permissions to users, service IDs, trusted profiles, and access groups in an account to work with a specific IAM-enabled service or resource instance, manage a resource group, or complete account management tasks.Access policies determine the level of access that users in your IBM Cloud account have to resources across the IBM Cloud platform. A policy assigns a user one or more roles that define the scope of access to a single service or to a set of services and resources that are organized together in a resource group. Each service in IBM Cloud might require its own set of access policies.

IAM, or Identity and Access Management, is a service provided by IBM Cloud that enables you to securely authenticate users for platform services and control access to resources across the IBM Cloud platform. IAM access policies are used to assign users, service IDs, and trusted profiles access to the resources within your account. IAM-enabled services are organized into resource groups within your account, and access to these services is given by using IAM access policies. IAM access policies are made up of a subject, target, and role. The subject is the who that has the access, the target is the resource to which you want to provide access, and the role defines the level of access or allowed actions on the target of the policy.
What is the difference between IBM Cloudant legacy and IAM access controls?

IBM Cloudant legacy access to each service instance requires its own set of credentials.
It uses HTTP basic authentication with credentials that aren't bound to an individual user or service.   IAM (Identity and Access Management) centrally managed access management across IBM Cloud. It allows a user or service to access many different resources by using the same set of credentials (for example, same username and password or IAM API key).

Designed for professionals with three or more years of experience working as cloud architects, [IBM Certified Advanced Architect - Cloud v1](https://www.ibm.com/training/path/ibmcloudadvancedarchitect) extends and validates your capabilities.  IBM Cloud Professional Developer

Engage technical skills and strategic vision to co-create with your client as their technical consultant with the [IBM Certified Professional Sales Engineer v1](https://www.ibm.com/training/certification/C0010200). Use public, hybrid, and multicloud solutions to get the technical win. IBM Cloud Sales Engineers possess a breadth of architecture experience, technical leadership skills, and knowledge in multiple technologies, industries, and platforms, with depth in IBM Cloud technologies and offerings.





 IBM Cloud Security Engineer Specialty

IBM Cloud ensures security readiness by adhering to security policies that are driven by best practices in IBM for systems, networking, and secure engineering. These policies include practices such as source code scanning, dynamic scanning, threat modeling, and penetration testing. IBM Cloud follows the IBM Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) process for security incident management. See the [IBM Security Vulnerability Management (PSIRT)](https://www.ibm.com/support/pages/ibm-security-vulnerability-management) site for details.

In addition to the regular penetration testing conducted by IBM and our partners, customers may conduct penetration testing of their VPC or Classic Infrastructure resources on IBM Cloud. Prior authorization to do so is not required by IBM Cloud. IBM Cloud customers under an active NDA can request a copy of a penetration testing executive summary by [opening a support case](https://cloud.ibm.com/unifiedsupport/supportcenter).
